title: The Astadhyayi
author: panini
attributionNote: Composed by Panini, of whom little is known beyond the work itself, which names him in its closing verse and describes the language of his own region as one of its objects.
description: The Astadhyayi describes Sanskrit in almost four thousand rules, ordered so that each rule applies after the ones before it and is overridden by the ones after. It gives the sounds, the morphology and the composition of the language, defines the technical operations by which forms are derived, and closes with rules for Vedic forms. Written in aphorisms of extraordinary economy, it is the founding work of Indian linguistics.
historicalContext: Panini's grammar set the vocabulary of all later Sanskrit grammar and of Sanskrit literary culture, and its rule-ordering and formal style have been read by modern linguists as an early formal grammar. It survives as the centre of a tradition that runs through Katyayana's varttikas and Patanjali's Mahabhashya.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit sutras of all eight chapters in the transliteration GRETIL publishes, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation; the rules are unexpanded and are read with the traditional aids.
